source.text: וִיהוֹרָ֣ם בֶּן־אַחְאָ֗ב מָלַ֤ךְ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּשֹׁ֣מְר֔וֹן בִּשְׁנַת֙ שְׁמֹנֶ֣ה עֶשְׂרֵ֔ה לִיהוֹשָׁפָ֖ט מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה וַיִּמְלֹ֖ךְ שְׁתֵּים־עֶשְׂרֵ֥ה שָׁנָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And Jehoram son of Ahab reigned over Israel in Samaria in year eighteen of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and he reigned twelve years.

en.L: And Jehoram son of Ahab reigned over Israel in Samaria in the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and he reigned twelve years.
en.B: In the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, Jehoram son of Ahab became king over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned twelve years.
en.R: Jehoram son of Ahab became king over Israel in the eighteenth year that Jehoshaphat was king of Judah. Jehoram ruled over Israel from Samaria for twelve years.

decisions.choice: Jehoram son of Ahab: Ahab's second son to rule Israel, also called Joram
decisions.reason: Jehoram followed his brother Ahaziah, who died without a son (1:17). The shorter form of his name, Joram, is used for him later (8:16; 9:14). He is a different man from Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat, who ruled Judah at about the same time (8:16).

decisions.choice: the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat: a date counted differently from 1:17
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 1:17 dates Jehoram's accession to the second year of Jehoram of Judah, Jehoshaphat's son. The two dates probably reflect a time when Jehoshaphat and his son ruled Judah together, so that a year could be counted from either reign. The text does not explain the difference.

decisions.choice: reigned (Literal); became king ... and he reigned (Balanced); became king ... ruled (Readable)
decisions.reason: The accession formula, worded at each level as throughout Kings (1 Kings 16:29). Balanced puts the date first, as the formula usually does; Readable splits it into two sentences.

source.text: וַיַּעֲשֶׂ֤ה הָרַע֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה רַ֕ק לֹ֥א כְאָבִ֖יו וּכְאִמּ֑וֹ וַיָּ֨סַר֙ אֶת־מַצְּבַ֣ת הַבַּ֔עַל אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה אָבִֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And he did the evil in [the] eyes of Yahweh, only not like his father and like his mother; and he removed [the] standing stone of the Baal which his father made.

en.L: And he did the evil in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, only not like his father and like his mother; and he removed the standing stone of the Baal that his father had made.
en.B: He did what was evil in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, though not like his father and mother. He removed the standing stone of Baal that his father had made.
en.R: He did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was evil, but he was not as bad as his father and mother had been. He took away the stone pillar for the god Baal that his father had set up.

decisions.choice: his father and his mother: Ahab and Jezebel
decisions.reason: Ahab built a temple and altar for Baal in Samaria (1 Kings 16:32-33), and Jezebel supported Baal's prophets (1 Kings 18:19). Jezebel was still alive in Jehoram's reign (9:22, 30).

decisions.choice: the standing stone of the Baal: a sacred stone set up in Baal's honor
decisions.reason: A standing stone was an upright stone that marked a place of worship and stood for the god's presence. Removing it was a partial reform. Baal's temple stayed, and Jehu later destroyed a standing stone of Baal there (10:26-27), so Baal's worship had not ended.

decisions.choice: did the evil in [the] eyes of / did what was evil in the sight of / did what the LORD said was evil
decisions.reason: The verdict formula, worded at each level as throughout Kings (1 Kings 16:19).

decisions.choice: stone pillar for the god Baal
decisions.reason: Readable uses its usual words for standing stones and says who Baal was (1 Kings 16:31).

source.text: רַ֠ק בְּחַטֹּ֞אות יָרָבְעָ֧ם בֶּֽן־נְבָ֛ט אֲשֶׁר־הֶחֱטִ֥יא אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל דָּבֵ֑ק לֹא־סָ֖ר מִמֶּֽנָּה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Only to [the] sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat which he made sin Israel he clung; not he turned from it.

en.L: Only, to the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, which he made Israel sin, he clung; he did not turn from them.
en.B: Yet he held on to the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, by which he led Israel to sin; he did not turn away from them.
en.R: But he kept on committing the sins by which Jeroboam son of Nebat led Israel into sin. He did not stop.

decisions.choice: the sins of Jeroboam which he made Israel sin: the calf shrines at Bethel and Dan
decisions.reason: Jeroboam set up golden calves at Bethel and Dan and led Israel to worship there (1 Kings 12:28-33). Kings judges every king of Israel by this sin. Jehoram removed one sign of Baal worship but kept Jeroboam's shrines.

decisions.choice: clung: held fast to
decisions.reason: The verb means to stick to something closely. It is the word used for holding fast to Yahweh (Deuteronomy 10:20); here Jehoram holds fast to Jeroboam's sins instead.

decisions.choice: from it: from those sins
decisions.reason: The pronoun is singular. It treats Jeroboam's sins as one whole, the worship he set up.

decisions.choice: made Israel sin (Literal); led Israel to sin (Balanced); led Israel into sin (Readable)
decisions.reason: The formula of the sin of Jeroboam keeps one wording at each level through Kings, as set at 1 Kings 14:16: "made Israel sin" (Literal), "led Israel to sin" (Balanced), "led Israel into sin" (Readable). Later uses in this book refer back here.

source.text: וּמֵישַׁ֥ע מֶֽלֶךְ־מוֹאָ֖ב הָיָ֣ה נֹקֵ֑ד וְהֵשִׁ֤יב לְמֶֽלֶךְ־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מֵאָה־אֶ֣לֶף כָּרִ֔ים וּמֵ֥אָה אֶ֖לֶף אֵילִ֥ים צָֽמֶר׃

records.literal_gloss: And Mesha king of Moab was a sheep-breeder, and he would deliver to [the] king of Israel a hundred thousand lambs and a hundred thousand rams, wool.

en.L: And Mesha king of Moab was a sheep breeder, and he used to deliver to the king of Israel 100,000 lambs and 100,000 rams, [their] wool.
en.B: Mesha king of Moab raised sheep, and he used to pay the king of Israel 100,000 lambs and the wool of 100,000 rams.
en.R: Mesha, the king of Moab, raised large flocks of sheep. Every year he had to give the king of Israel 100,000 lambs and the wool of 100,000 rams.

decisions.choice: sheep breeder: an owner of large flocks
decisions.reason: The word names someone who raises sheep on a large scale. It is used of the prophet Amos (Amos 1:1). Moab's high plain east of the Dead Sea was good grazing land.

decisions.choice: he would deliver: a tribute paid again and again
decisions.reason: The verb form describes a repeated action. Moab had been under Israel's rule and paid a regular tribute in animals and wool. A Moabite inscription set up by Mesha himself, the Moabite Stone found in 1868, says that Omri and his son had oppressed Moab and that Mesha freed his land.

decisions.choice: rams, wool: the wool of the rams
alternatives: 100,000 lambs and 100,000 rams, with their wool
decisions.reason: The word "wool" stands at the end without a link word. It most likely means the wool of the 100,000 rams, though it could mean that both lambs and rams were paid with their wool.

decisions.choice: Every year he had to give
decisions.reason: Readable makes the repeated payment explicit. The Hebrew does not say how often it was paid, so "every year" goes beyond the text.

source.text: וַיְהִ֖י כְּמ֣וֹת אַחְאָ֑ב וַיִּפְשַׁ֥ע מֶֽלֶךְ־מוֹאָ֖ב בְּמֶ֥לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, as died Ahab, and rebelled [the] king of Moab against [the] king of Israel.

en.L: And it was, when Ahab died, that the king of Moab rebelled against the king of Israel.
en.B: But when Ahab died, the king of Moab rebelled against the king of Israel.
en.R: But after Ahab died, the king of Moab turned against the king of Israel and stopped paying.

decisions.choice: rebelled: the revolt already mentioned in 1:1
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 1:1 has already said that Moab rebelled after Ahab's death. The story now returns to it to tell how Israel tried to win Moab back.

decisions.choice: rebelled: broke away from the treaty
decisions.reason: The verb means to break faith with a lord or treaty partner. Here it means that Mesha refused to go on paying the tribute of verse 4.

decisions.choice: turned against ... and stopped paying
decisions.reason: Readable says what the rebellion meant in practice (m2).

source.text: וַיֵּצֵ֞א הַמֶּ֧לֶךְ יְהוֹרָ֛ם בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא מִשֹּׁמְר֑וֹן וַיִּפְקֹ֖ד אֶת־כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And went out the king Jehoram on the day the that from Samaria, and he mustered all Israel.

en.L: And King Jehoram went out from Samaria on that day, and he mustered all Israel.
en.B: So at that time King Jehoram marched out of Samaria and mustered all Israel.
en.R: So King Jehoram left Samaria at that time and called up the whole army of Israel.

decisions.choice: on that day: at that time
decisions.reason: "On that day" here means "at that time", when Moab rebelled, not a single day.

decisions.choice: mustered all Israel: counted and called up the fighting men
decisions.reason: The verb means to count or review, and here to gather the men fit for war.

decisions.choice: called up the whole army of Israel
decisions.reason: Readable says that "all Israel" here means the fighting men (m2).

source.text: וַיֵּ֡לֶךְ וַיִּשְׁלַח֩ אֶל־יְהוֹשָׁפָ֨ט מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָ֜ה לֵאמֹ֗ר מֶ֤לֶךְ מוֹאָב֙ פָּשַׁ֣ע בִּ֔י הֲתֵלֵ֥ךְ אִתִּ֛י אֶל־מוֹאָ֖ב לַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֶעֱלֶ֔ה כָּמ֧וֹנִי כָמ֛וֹךָ כְּעַמִּ֥י כְעַמֶּ֖ךָ כְּסוּסַ֥י כְּסוּסֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he went and sent to Jehoshaphat king of Judah saying, [the] king of Moab has rebelled against me; will you go with me against Moab for the battle? And he said, I will go up; as me as you, as my people as your people, as my horses as your horses.

en.L: And he went and sent to Jehoshaphat king of Judah, saying, "The king of Moab has rebelled against me. Will you go with me against Moab to battle?" And he said, "I will go up. As I [am], so [are] you; as my people, so your people; as my horses, so your horses."
en.B: He also sent word to Jehoshaphat king of Judah. "The king of Moab," he said, "has rebelled against me. Will you join me in battle against Moab?" Jehoshaphat answered, "I will go. I am as you are, my troops are as your troops, my horses as your horses."
en.R: He sent a message to Jehoshaphat, the king of Judah. It said, "The king of Moab has turned against me. Will you come with me and fight Moab?" Jehoshaphat answered, "I will go. I am with you all the way. My army and my horses are yours to command."

decisions.choice: as I am, so are you: the same pledge Jehoshaphat gave Ahab
decisions.reason: Jehoshaphat answers Ahab's son in the words he used to Ahab before the battle at Ramoth-gilead (1 Kings 22:4), where Ahab died. Here he adds "I will go up", and he does not ask for a word from Yahweh until the army is in trouble (verse 11), unlike 1 Kings 22:5.

decisions.choice: as I am, so are you ...: I am fully with you; all I have is at your disposal
decisions.reason: A set saying of alliance, as in 1 Kings 22:4: Jehoshaphat puts himself, his army and his chariot horses on the same footing as Jehoram's.

decisions.choice: my people: my army
decisions.reason: Here "people" means the fighting men a king leads into battle (1 Kings 22:4).

decisions.choice: the wording of 1 Kings 22:4
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable reuse the wording of 1 Kings 22:4 at each level, where the Hebrew is the same: Balanced "troops", Readable "army" and the saying explained. Balanced and Readable say "go" for "go up".

decisions.choice: Jehoshaphat answered
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker, as the context makes clear.

source.text: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אֵי־זֶ֥ה הַדֶּ֖רֶךְ נַעֲלֶ֑ה וַיֹּ֕אמֶר דֶּ֖רֶךְ מִדְבַּ֥ר אֱדֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, where? this the way [which] we will go up? And he said, [the] way of [the] wilderness of Edom.

en.L: And he said, "Which way shall we go up?" And he said, "The way of the wilderness of Edom."
en.B: Then he asked, "By which route shall we attack?" He answered, "By the road through the wilderness of Edom."
en.R: Then one king asked, "Which way should we go to attack?" The other answered, "We will go through the desert of Edom."

decisions.choice: he said ... he said: the speakers are not named
decisions.reason: The Hebrew does not say who asks and who answers. Either Jehoshaphat asks and Jehoram chooses the route, or the other way round. Both readings are possible.

decisions.choice: the way of the wilderness of Edom: around the south end of the Dead Sea
decisions.reason: This route led from Judah south around the Dead Sea and through the dry land of Edom, so that the army could enter Moab from the south rather than across the Jordan from the north. It was long and had little water (verse 9).

decisions.choice: go up: march to attack
decisions.reason: "Go up" is a common way of speaking of going out to war against a place.

decisions.choice: one king ... the other
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the two kings are speaking, without choosing which one is which (m1).

source.text: וַיֵּלֶךְ֩ מֶ֨לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל וּמֶֽלֶך־יְהוּדָה֙וּמֶ֣לֶךְ אֱד֔וֹם וַיָּסֹ֕בּוּ דֶּ֖רֶךְ שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֑ים וְלֹא־הָיָ֨ה מַ֧יִם לַֽמַּחֲנֶ֛ה וְלַבְּהֵמָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּרַגְלֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And went [the] king of Israel and [the] king of Judah and [the] king of Edom, and they went around a way of seven days, and not there was water for the camp and for the animals which [were] at their feet.

en.L: And the king of Israel and the king of Judah and the king of Edom went, and they went around on a way of seven days, and there was no water for the camp or for the animals that [were] at their feet.
en.B: So the king of Israel set out with the king of Judah and the king of Edom. After a roundabout march of seven days, there was no water left for the army or for the animals that followed them.
en.R: So the three kings, of Israel, Judah and Edom, set out together. They marched for seven days along a roundabout route. Then they ran out of water for the soldiers and for the animals that came with them.

decisions.choice: the king of Edom: a ruler under Judah's control
decisions.reason: In Jehoshaphat's time Edom had no king of its own but a deputy who served as king (1 Kings 22:48), and Edom broke free from Judah only later (8:20). This king of Edom was probably that ruler, joining the march as Judah's ally.

decisions.choice: they went around a way of seven days: they took a roundabout route for seven days
decisions.reason: The verb means to go around. The march went the long way round, through dry country, and lasted seven days.

decisions.choice: the animals at their feet: the animals that followed them
decisions.reason: "At their feet" means following behind them. These were the pack animals and the livestock that went with the army.

decisions.choice: the camp: the army in its camp
decisions.reason: The word for a camp is often used for the army itself.

decisions.choice: army / soldiers; followed them / came with them
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "camp" and "at their feet" mean (m3, m4).

source.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אֲהָ֕הּ כִּֽי־קָרָ֣א יְהוָ֗ה לִשְׁלֹ֨שֶׁת֙הַמְּלָכִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה לָתֵ֥ת אוֹתָ֖ם בְּיַד־מוֹאָֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: And said [the] king of Israel, alas! for has called Yahweh the three kings the these to give them into [the] hand of Moab.

en.L: And the king of Israel said, "Alas! For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has called these three kings to give them into the hand of Moab."
en.B: The king of Israel said, "How terrible! {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has called these three kings together to hand them over to Moab."
en.R: The king of Israel cried out, "This is terrible! {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has brought these three kings out here to let Moab defeat them!"

decisions.choice: alas! for: a cry of despair, then its reason
decisions.reason: The cry expresses dismay. The word after it gives the reason: the king believes the lack of water is Yahweh's doing.

decisions.choice: Yahweh has called these three kings to give them into the hand of Moab
decisions.reason: Jehoram blames Yahweh for the disaster, though he has not asked Yahweh anything before setting out. To give someone into another's hand means to let the enemy defeat them (verse 18). Elisha's answer will turn the same words around: Yahweh will give Moab into their hand.

decisions.choice: How terrible! / This is terrible!
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the cry "alas" in everyday words. Literal keeps "Alas".

decisions.choice: hand them over to Moab / let Moab defeat them
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "give into the hand" means, as in 1 Kings 20:13.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוֹשָׁפָ֗ט הַאֵ֨ין פֹּ֤ה נָבִיא֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה וְנִדְרְשָׁ֥ה אֶת־יְהוָ֖ה מֵאוֹת֑וֹ וַ֠יַּעַן אֶחָ֞ד מֵעַבְדֵ֤י מֶֽלֶךְ־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וַיֹּ֔אמֶר פֹּ֚ה אֱלִישָׁ֣ע בֶּן־שָׁפָ֔ט אֲשֶׁר־יָ֥צַק מַ֖יִם עַל־יְדֵ֥י אֵלִיָּֽהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Jehoshaphat, is there not here a prophet of Yahweh, and we may inquire of Yahweh from him? And answered one of [the] servants of [the] king of Israel and said, here [is] Elisha son of Shaphat, who poured water on [the] hands of Elijah.

en.L: And Jehoshaphat said, "Is there not here a prophet of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, that we may inquire of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} through him?" And one of the servants of the king of Israel answered and said, "Elisha son of Shaphat [is] here, who poured water on the hands of Elijah."
en.B: But Jehoshaphat asked, "Is there no prophet of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} here, through whom we can inquire of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}?" One of the king of Israel's officials answered, "Elisha son of Shaphat is here, the man who used to pour water on Elijah's hands."
en.R: But Jehoshaphat asked, "Is there not a prophet of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} here? We could ask {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} what to do through him." One of the king of Israel's officials answered, "Elisha son of Shaphat is here. He was Elijah's personal helper."

decisions.choice: is there not here a prophet of Yahweh?: Jehoshaphat's question at Ramoth-gilead
decisions.reason: Jehoshaphat asked almost the same question before the battle in which Ahab died (1 Kings 22:7). Then as now, he wants a true prophet of Yahweh to say what Yahweh will do.

decisions.choice: inquire of Yahweh through him: ask Yahweh for guidance by a prophet
decisions.reason: Kings asked Yahweh before or during a war whether to go on and whether they would win, usually through a prophet (1 Kings 22:5, 8).

decisions.choice: who poured water on the hands of Elijah: who served Elijah as his attendant
decisions.reason: A servant poured water over his master's hands for washing. The phrase means that Elisha was Elijah's personal attendant (1 Kings 19:21). It tells the kings that Elisha carries on Elijah's work (2:9-15).

decisions.choice: the servants of the king of Israel: his officials
decisions.reason: The king's "servants" are the officers of his court and army.

decisions.choice: officials
decisions.reason: As in these books, the king's servants are "officials" at Balanced and Readable; Literal keeps "servants".

decisions.choice: He used to be Elijah's personal helper
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture of pouring water means (m3). Balanced keeps the picture.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ יְה֣וֹשָׁפָ֔ט יֵ֥שׁ אוֹת֖וֹ דְּבַר־יְהוָ֑ה וַיֵּרְד֣וּ אֵלָ֗יו מֶ֧לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל וִיהוֹשָׁפָ֖ט וּמֶ֥לֶךְ אֱדֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Jehoshaphat, there is with him [the] word of Yahweh; and went down to him [the] king of Israel and Jehoshaphat and [the] king of Edom.

en.L: And Jehoshaphat said, "The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is with him." And the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat and the king of Edom went down to him.
en.B: Jehoshaphat said, "The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is with him." Then the king of Israel went down to him, with Jehoshaphat and the king of Edom.
en.R: Jehoshaphat said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} speaks through him." So the king of Israel, Jehoshaphat and the king of Edom went down to see Elisha.

decisions.choice: the word of Yahweh is with him: Yahweh speaks through him
decisions.reason: Jehoshaphat recognizes Elisha as a true prophet, one to whom Yahweh gives his message.

decisions.choice: they went down to him: the kings go to the prophet
decisions.reason: The three kings do not summon Elisha but go to him themselves. It shows their need, and the respect they give him as Yahweh's prophet.

decisions.choice: The LORD speaks through him
decisions.reason: Readable says what "the word of the LORD is with him" means (m1).

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֱלִישָׁ֜ע אֶל־מֶ֤לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מַה־לִּ֣י וָלָ֔ךְ לֵ֚ךְ אֶל־נְבִיאֵ֣י אָבִ֔יךָ וְאֶל־נְבִיאֵ֖י אִמֶּ֑ךָ וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אַ֗ל כִּֽי־קָרָ֤א יְהוָה֙ לִשְׁלֹ֨שֶׁת֙ הַמְּלָכִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה לָתֵ֥ת אוֹתָ֖ם בְּיַד־מוֹאָֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Elisha to [the] king of Israel, what [is] to me and to you? Go to [the] prophets of your father and to [the] prophets of your mother. And said to him [the] king of Israel, no, for has called Yahweh the three kings the these to give them into [the] hand of Moab.

en.L: And Elisha said to the king of Israel, "What [is there] to me and to you? Go to the prophets of your father and to the prophets of your mother." And the king of Israel said to him, "No, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has called these three kings to give them into the hand of Moab."
en.B: Elisha said to the king of Israel, "What do you and I have to do with each other? Go to your father's prophets and your mother's prophets." But the king of Israel said to him, "No, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has called these three kings together to hand them over to Moab."
en.R: Elisha said to the king of Israel, "Why should I help you? Go to the prophets your father and mother listened to!" But the king of Israel answered, "No! It is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} who has brought these three kings out here to let Moab defeat them."

decisions.choice: what is there to me and to you?: we have nothing to do with each other
decisions.reason: The question refuses a claim on the speaker (Judges 11:12; 1 Kings 17:18). Elisha owes the king of Israel nothing.

decisions.choice: the prophets of your father and of your mother: the prophets Ahab and Jezebel kept
decisions.reason: Jezebel supported hundreds of prophets of Baal and Asherah (1 Kings 18:19), and Ahab kept four hundred prophets who told him what he wanted to hear (1 Kings 22:6). Elisha tells Jehoram to ask them, since he trusts them.

decisions.choice: no, for: do not send us away, because
decisions.reason: Jehoram does not argue with the charge. His "no" begs Elisha not to refuse, because only Yahweh can help in the trouble he believes Yahweh has brought (verse 10).

decisions.choice: What do you and I have to do with each other? / Why should I help you?
decisions.reason: Balanced turns the idiom into a plain question; Readable gives its point (m1).

decisions.choice: the prophets your father and mother listened to
decisions.reason: Readable joins the two phrases and says what they mean (m2).

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלִישָׁ֗ע חַי־יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָמַ֣דְתִּי לְפָנָ֔יו כִּ֗י לוּלֵ֛י פְּנֵ֛י יְהוֹשָׁפָ֥ט מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָ֖ה אֲנִ֣י נֹשֵׂ֑א אִם־אַבִּ֥יט אֵלֶ֖יךָ וְאִם־אֶרְאֶֽךָּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Elisha, [as] lives Yahweh of hosts, whom I stand before his face, that if not [the] face of Jehoshaphat king of Judah I [am] lifting up, if I would look to you and if I would see you,

en.L: And Elisha said, "[As] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts lives, before whom I stand, were it not that I lift up the face of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, I would not look at you or see you.
en.B: Elisha said, "As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies lives, whom I serve, if I did not respect Jehoshaphat king of Judah, I would not look at you or even notice you.
en.R: Elisha said, "I serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies. As surely as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} lives, I would not even look at you if Jehoshaphat, the king of Judah, were not here. I respect him.

decisions.choice: as Yahweh of hosts lives, before whom I stand: a solemn oath by the one Elisha serves
decisions.reason: Elisha swears in the words Elijah used (1 Kings 17:1; 18:15). To "stand before" someone is to serve him, as an attendant stands ready before a king. "Hosts" means armies: Yahweh rules all the powers of heaven and earth.

decisions.choice: lift up the face of Jehoshaphat: show regard for Jehoshaphat
decisions.reason: To lift someone's face is to receive him with favor. Elisha helps only for the sake of Jehoshaphat, Judah's faithful king (1 Kings 22:43).

decisions.choice: if I would look at you: I would not look at you
decisions.reason: In an oath, "if I do this" leaves a curse unspoken and means "I will not do this" (1 Kings 17:1). Elisha would not so much as look at Jehoram.

decisions.choice: the LORD of hosts (Literal); the LORD of Armies (Balanced, Readable); before whom I stand / whom I serve
decisions.reason: The oath is worded at each level as in 1 Kings 18:15, where the Hebrew is the same.

decisions.choice: respect
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "lift up the face" means (m2). Readable reorders the sentence and puts the reason last to keep it short.

source.text: וְעַתָּ֖ה קְחוּ־לִ֣י מְנַגֵּ֑ן וְהָיָה֙ כְּנַגֵּ֣ן הַֽמְנַגֵּ֔ן וַתְּהִ֥י עָלָ֖יו יַד־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And now fetch for me a musician. And it was, as played the musician, and was on him [the] hand of Yahweh.

en.L: But now bring me a musician." And it was, as the musician played, that the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came upon him.
en.B: But now bring me a musician." While the musician was playing, the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came on Elisha.
en.R: Now bring me someone to play music." While the musician was playing, the power of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came on Elisha.

decisions.choice: a musician: someone who plays a stringed instrument
decisions.reason: The verb means to play on strings, as David played the lyre for Saul (1 Samuel 16:16, 23). Music went with prophecy in Israel (1 Samuel 10:5; 1 Chronicles 25:1).

decisions.choice: the hand of Yahweh came on him: Yahweh's power took hold of him to speak
decisions.reason: The hand stands for power. The phrase is used when Yahweh moves a prophet to act or to receive a message (1 Kings 18:46; Ezekiel 1:3). The message follows in verse 16.

decisions.choice: the power of the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable says what the hand stands for (m2).

decisions.choice: Elisha
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Elisha for "him", for clarity.

source.text: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה עָשֹׂ֛ה הַנַּ֥חַל הַזֶּ֖ה גֵּבִ֥ים׀גֵּבִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, thus says Yahweh, make the wadi the this ditches, ditches.

en.L: And he said, "Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: 'Make this wadi [into] ditches, ditches.'
en.B: Then he said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: 'Dig ditch after ditch in this streambed.'
en.R: Then Elisha said, "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: 'Dig many ditches in this dry streambed.'

decisions.choice: make: a command to dig the ditches
alternatives: This wadi will be made full of pools
decisions.reason: The verb form can give a command or simply describe what will happen. Read as a command, the kings must dig ditches to hold the water Yahweh will send (verse 17). Read as a description, Yahweh himself says he will make the wadi full of pools. The command fits the instructions that follow, but the other reading is possible.

decisions.choice: ditches, ditches: many ditches
decisions.reason: Repeating a word shows a great number: the wadi is to be full of them.

decisions.choice: wadi: a valley or streambed dry for most of the year
decisions.reason: A wadi carries water only after rain. The army is camped in or near one on the border of Moab.

decisions.choice: Thus says the LORD / The LORD says this / This is what the LORD says
decisions.reason: The messenger formula, worded at each level as in these books.

decisions.choice: streambed / dry streambed
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable describe the wadi (m3). Literal keeps the word "wadi".

source.text: כִּֽי־כֹ֣ה׀אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה לֹֽא־תִרְא֥וּ ר֨וּחַ֙ וְלֹֽא־תִרְא֣וּ גֶ֔שֶׁם וְהַנַּ֥חַל הַה֖וּא יִמָּ֣לֵא מָ֑יִם וּשְׁתִיתֶ֛ם אַתֶּ֥ם וּמִקְנֵיכֶ֖ם וּֽבְהֶמְתְּכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: For thus says Yahweh, not you will see wind and not you will see rain, and the wadi the that will be filled [with] water, and you will drink, you and your livestock and your animals.

en.L: For thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: 'You will not see wind, and you will not see rain, yet that wadi will be filled [with] water, and you will drink, you and your livestock and your animals.'
en.B: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says this: 'You will see no wind and no rain, yet that streambed will fill with water, and you will drink, you and your livestock and your pack animals.'
en.R: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: 'You will not feel any wind or see any rain. Yet that streambed will fill with water. Then you and your cattle and your other animals will have water to drink.'

decisions.choice: no wind and no rain, yet water: Yahweh's own gift
decisions.reason: Wind and rain would come before a storm. The water will come without any sign of a storm where they are, so that they know it is Yahweh's doing.

decisions.choice: your livestock and your animals: the herds and the beasts of burden
decisions.reason: The first word names livestock kept as property, herds and flocks taken along for food; the second names animals in general, here the pack animals of verse 9.

decisions.choice: pack animals / other animals
decisions.reason: Balanced names the animals of verse 9 that carried the army's loads; Readable keeps it general.

decisions.choice: feel any wind
decisions.reason: Readable says "feel" for wind, which cannot be seen. Literal and Balanced keep the Hebrew's single verb "see".

source.text: וְנָקַ֥ל זֹ֖את בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְנָתַ֥ן אֶת־מוֹאָ֖ב בְּיֶדְכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And it is light this in [the] eyes of Yahweh, and he will give Moab into your hand.

en.L: And this is a light thing in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will give Moab into your hand.
en.B: This is only a small thing in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will also hand Moab over to you.
en.R: And this is easy for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to do. He will also let you defeat Moab.

decisions.choice: a light thing in the eyes of Yahweh: easy for Yahweh
decisions.reason: "Light" means of little weight. Giving water in the desert is a small thing for Yahweh; he will do more.

decisions.choice: he will give Moab into your hand: the answer to the king's fear
decisions.reason: Jehoram feared that Yahweh would give the three kings into the hand of Moab (verses 10, 13). Yahweh will give Moab into theirs instead.

decisions.choice: hand Moab over to you / let you defeat Moab
decisions.reason: As in verse 10, Balanced and Readable say what "give into your hand" means.

source.text: וְהִכִּיתֶ֞ם כָּל־עִ֤יר מִבְצָר֙ וְכָל־עִ֣יר מִבְח֔וֹר וְכָל־עֵ֥ץ טוֹב֙ תַּפִּ֔ילוּ וְכָל־מַעְיְנֵי־מַ֖יִם תִּסְתֹּ֑מוּ וְכֹל֙ הַחֶלְקָ֣ה הַטּוֹבָ֔ה תַּכְאִ֖בוּ בָּאֲבָנִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will strike every city of fortification and every city of choice, and every tree good you will fell, and all springs of water you will stop up, and every portion the good you will ruin with stones.

en.L: And you will strike every fortified city and every choice city, and every good tree you will fell, and all the springs of water you will stop up, and every good plot [of land] you will ruin with stones."
en.B: You will strike down every fortified town and every major town. You will cut down every good tree, block every spring of water, and ruin every good field with stones."
en.R: You will conquer every town with walls and every important town. You will cut down every good tree, block up every spring, and ruin every good field by covering it with stones."

decisions.choice: fortified city ... choice city: every strong and every important town
decisions.reason: The two phrases sound alike in Hebrew. A "choice" city is a fine or leading one. Together they mean all the towns that mattered.

decisions.choice: you will strike ... fell ... stop up ... ruin: a prediction that also directs
decisions.reason: The verbs say what the army will do. Coming from Yahweh's prophet, they also tell the kings what to do (verse 25).

decisions.choice: every good tree you will fell: total ruin of the land
decisions.reason: Cutting the trees, stopping the springs and covering the fields with stones would leave Moab unable to support its people for years. The law forbade cutting down fruit trees while besieging a city (Deuteronomy 20:19-20). The text does not say how the prophet's word relates to that law.

decisions.choice: major town / town with walls; important town
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "fortified" and "choice" in common words (m1).

decisions.choice: field
decisions.reason: The word means a portion or plot of land; Balanced and Readable say "field", the cultivated land the stones would spoil.

source.text: וַיְהִ֤י בַבֹּ֨קֶר֙ כַּעֲל֣וֹת הַמִּנְחָ֔ה וְהִנֵּה־מַ֥יִם בָּאִ֖ים מִדֶּ֣רֶךְ אֱד֑וֹם וַתִּמָּלֵ֥א הָאָ֖רֶץ אֶת־הַמָּֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was in the morning, as went up the offering, and look, water coming from [the] way of Edom, and was filled the land [with] the water.

en.L: And it was in the morning, at the going up of the offering, and look, water was coming from the way of Edom, and the land was filled [with] the water.
en.B: The next morning, about the time of the morning offering, water suddenly came flowing from the direction of Edom, and the land was filled with water.
en.R: The next morning, at the time when the morning sacrifice was offered, water suddenly came flowing from the direction of Edom. Soon the whole area was full of water.

decisions.choice: as the offering went up: at the time of the regular morning offering
decisions.reason: The offering named here was the daily one made at the temple in the morning (Exodus 29:38-42). Elijah's prayer on Mount Carmel came at the time of the evening offering (1 Kings 18:36). The time ties Yahweh's answer to the hour of worship.

decisions.choice: water coming from the way of Edom: water flowing down from the south
decisions.reason: Rain on the high ground of Edom can send a sudden flood down dry valleys far away, where no storm is seen. The text presents the water as Yahweh's promised gift (verse 17).

decisions.choice: look: a sudden sight
decisions.reason: The word draws attention to something seen suddenly, from the point of view of those who saw it.

decisions.choice: the morning offering / the morning sacrifice
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the offering by its time (m1), as 1 Kings 18:29 and 36 name the evening offering.

decisions.choice: The next morning
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say that this was the morning after Elisha spoke.

source.text: וְכָל־מוֹאָב֙ שָֽׁמְע֔וּ כִּֽי־עָל֥וּ הַמְּלָכִ֖ים לְהִלָּ֣חֶם בָּ֑ם וַיִּצָּעֲק֗וּ מִכֹּ֨ל חֹגֵ֤ר חֲגֹרָה֙ וָמַ֔עְלָה וַיַּעַמְד֖וּ עַֽל־הַגְּבֽוּל׃

records.literal_gloss: And all Moab had heard that had come up the kings to fight against them, and they were called out, from all girding a belt and upward, and they stood at the border.

en.L: And all Moab had heard that the kings had come up to fight against them, and they were called out, from all who could put on a belt and upward, and they took their stand at the border.
en.B: Meanwhile all Moab had heard that the kings had come to fight against them. Everyone old enough to put on a sword belt, and older, was called out, and they took up positions at the border.
en.R: By now all the Moabites had heard that the kings had come to fight against them. So every man old enough to fight, young and old, was called up. They went and stood ready at the border.

decisions.choice: had heard: before the water came
decisions.reason: The verb form looks back. While the allied army was marching, Moab had already gathered its men.

decisions.choice: all girding a belt and upward: every man old enough to bear arms
decisions.reason: A soldier put on a belt to carry his sword. "And upward" means everyone of that age and older.

decisions.choice: they were called out: summoned to war
decisions.reason: The verb means to cry out; in this form it means to be summoned by a call to arms (Judges 6:34-35).

decisions.choice: sword belt / old enough to fight
decisions.reason: Balanced says what the belt was for; Readable says what the idiom means (m2).

source.text: וַיַּשְׁכִּ֣ימוּ בַבֹּ֔קֶר וְהַשֶּׁ֖מֶשׁ זָרְחָ֣ה עַל־הַמָּ֑יִם וַיִּרְא֨וּ מוֹאָ֥ב מִנֶּ֛גֶד אֶת־הַמַּ֖יִם אֲדֻמִּ֥ים כַּדָּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they rose early in the morning, and the sun shone on the water, and saw Moab from opposite the water red like blood.

en.L: And they rose early in the morning, and the sun had risen on the water, and Moab saw the water opposite [them] red like blood.
en.B: Early in the morning they got up, and the sun was shining on the water. To the Moabites facing it, the water looked as red as blood.
en.R: Early the next morning, when the Moabites got up, the sun was shining on the water. From where they stood, the water looked red like blood.

decisions.choice: Moab ... red like blood: a play on the name Edom
decisions.reason: In Hebrew, "Edom", "red" and "blood" sound alike. The water came from Edom (verse 20) and looked red to Moab, which led the Moabites to think of blood.

decisions.choice: the sun shone on the water: the early light made it look red
decisions.reason: The low morning sun, perhaps with red earth in the water, gave it a red color seen from a distance. The Moabites did not know that water had come (verse 17).

decisions.choice: saw ... from opposite: saw it from a distance, facing it
decisions.reason: The Moabites saw the water from their positions across from the allied camp.

decisions.choice: looked as red as blood
decisions.reason: Balanced says the water "looked" red, since the Moabites were wrong about what they saw (verse 23).

source.text: וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ דָּ֣ם זֶ֔ה הָחֳרֵ֤ב נֶֽחֶרְבוּ֙ הַמְּלָכִ֔ים וַיַּכּ֖וּ אִ֣ישׁ אֶת־רֵעֵ֑הוּ וְעַתָּ֥ה לַשָּׁלָ֖ל מוֹאָֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: And they said, blood [is] this; surely have fought each other the kings, and they have struck each his neighbor; and now, to the plunder, Moab!

en.L: And they said, "This [is] blood! The kings have surely fought each other, and they have struck each other down. And now, to the plunder, Moab!"
en.B: They said, "This is blood! The kings must have fought one another and killed each other. Now, Moab, to the plunder!"
en.R: They said, "That is blood! The kings must have turned on each other and killed one another. Come on, Moabites! Let us go and take everything they have!"

decisions.choice: have surely fought each other: the kings must have turned their swords on each other
decisions.reason: The verb is formed from the word for sword, and it is doubled for emphasis. The Moabites are sure of what they think they see.

decisions.choice: the kings have struck each other: allies falling out
decisions.reason: An alliance of rival kingdoms could break apart in a quarrel (Judges 7:22; 1 Samuel 14:20). The Moabites think this has happened.

decisions.choice: each his neighbor: one another
decisions.reason: "Each ... his neighbor" is the Hebrew way of saying "one another".

decisions.choice: to the plunder, Moab!: a call to go and seize the spoil
decisions.reason: Moab is addressed as one army. Plunder was what an army took from a defeated enemy's camp.

decisions.choice: Come on, Moabites! Let us go and take everything they have!
decisions.reason: Readable turns the short cry into plain sentences that say what it calls for (m4).

source.text: וַיָּבֹאוּ֮ אֶל־מַחֲנֵ֣ה יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ וַיָּקֻ֤מוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וַיַּכּ֣וּ אֶת־מוֹאָ֔ב וַיָּנֻ֖סוּ מִפְּנֵיהֶ֑ם וַיַּכּוּ־בָ֔הּ וְהַכּ֖וֹת אֶת־מוֹאָֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: And they came to [the] camp of Israel, and rose up Israel and struck Moab, and they fled from before them; and they struck in it, and striking Moab.

en.L: And they came to the camp of Israel, and Israel rose up and struck Moab, and they fled before them; and they struck in it, striking Moab.
en.B: But when the Moabites reached the camp of Israel, the Israelites sprang up and attacked them, and they fled. The Israelites pushed on into the land, striking down the Moabites.
en.R: But when the Moabites came to Israel's camp, the Israelites jumped up and attacked them, and the Moabites ran away. The Israelites chased them into their own land and kept on killing them.

decisions.choice: they struck in it: Israel pressed on into Moab's land, striking the Moabites
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text, as its vowels read it, says "they struck in it", that is, Israel fought on inside Moab. The written letters can also be read "they went into it", and the ancient Greek translation has "they went in". Either way Israel advanced into Moab, cutting down the Moabites as it went.

decisions.choice: and striking Moab: striking them as they went
decisions.reason: The verb form without a subject describes the action that went with the advance.

decisions.choice: Israel: the allied army
decisions.reason: "Israel" here names the whole army in Israel's camp, Judah's and Edom's men with it.

decisions.choice: into the land / into their own land
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "it" refers to: the land of Moab.

source.text: וְהֶעָרִ֣ים יַהֲרֹ֡סוּ וְכָל־חֶלְקָ֣ה ט֠וֹבָה יַשְׁלִ֨יכוּ אִישׁ־אַבְנ֜וֹ וּמִלְא֗וּהָ וְכָל־מַעְיַן־מַ֤יִם יִסְתֹּ֨מוּ֙ וְכָל־עֵֽץ־ט֣וֹב יַפִּ֔ילוּ עַד־הִשְׁאִ֧יר אֲבָנֶ֛יהָ בַּקִּ֖יר חֲרָ֑שֶׂת וַיָּסֹ֥בּוּ הַקַּלָּעִ֖ים וַיַּכּֽוּהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And the cities they tore down, and every good portion they threw each his stone and filled it, and every spring of water they stopped up, and every good tree they felled, until he left its stones in Kir-hareseth; and went around the slingers and struck it.

en.L: And they tore down the cities, and on every good plot [of land] each threw his stone, and they filled it, and they stopped up every spring of water, and they felled every good tree, until only its stones were left in Kir-hareseth; and the slingers surrounded [it] and struck it.
en.B: They tore down the towns, and each man threw a stone on every good field until it was covered. They blocked every spring of water and cut down every good tree. At last only Kir-hareseth was left with its stones standing, and the slingers surrounded it and attacked it.
en.R: They destroyed the towns. Every soldier threw a stone onto each good field until the fields were covered. They blocked up every spring and cut down every good tree. In the end only the walls of Kir-hareseth were still standing. But soldiers with slings surrounded that city and attacked it.

decisions.choice: towns, fields, springs, trees: Elisha's word carried out
decisions.reason: The army does each of the things Elisha said it would (verse 19), in a different order.

decisions.choice: until he left its stones in Kir-hareseth: until only Kir-hareseth stood
alternatives: until only the stones of Kir-hareseth were left
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is short and hard: literally "until he left its stones in Kir-hareseth". It most likely means that nothing was left standing except the stone walls of Kir-hareseth. Kir-hareseth was Moab's chief stronghold (Isaiah 16:7, 11).

decisions.choice: the slingers: soldiers armed with slings
decisions.reason: A sling threw stones with great force and could reach defenders on a wall (Judges 20:16).

decisions.choice: until only its stones were left
decisions.reason: Literal gives the impersonal "he left" as a passive, since no person is meant (m2).

decisions.choice: the walls of Kir-hareseth
decisions.reason: Readable says what "its stones" refers to, the city's stone walls (m2).

source.text: וַיַּרְא֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ מוֹאָ֔ב כִּֽי־חָזַ֥ק מִמֶּ֖נּוּ הַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה וַיִּקַּ֣ח א֠וֹתוֹ שְׁבַע־מֵא֨וֹת אִ֜ישׁ שֹׁ֣לֵֽף חֶ֗רֶב לְהַבְקִ֛יעַ אֶל־מֶ֥לֶךְ אֱד֖וֹם וְלֹ֥א יָכֹֽלוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And saw [the] king of Moab that was too strong for him the battle, and he took with him seven hundred men drawing sword, to break through to [the] king of Edom; and not they were able.

en.L: And the king of Moab saw that the battle was too strong for him, and he took with him 700 men who drew the sword, to break through to the king of Edom; but they were not able.
en.B: When the king of Moab saw that the battle was going against him, he took with him 700 swordsmen to try to break through to the king of Edom, but they failed.
en.R: The king of Moab saw that he was losing the battle. So he took 700 soldiers armed with swords and tried to break through the enemy lines to reach the king of Edom. But they could not get through.

decisions.choice: the battle was too strong for him: he was losing
decisions.reason: The phrase means that the fighting had gone beyond what the king could hold.

decisions.choice: to break through to the king of Edom: to attack where the allies were weakest
decisions.reason: The text does not say why Mesha chose Edom's position. It may have been the weakest part of the siege lines, or he may have hoped that Edom, the least willing ally, would give way.

decisions.choice: men drawing sword: armed fighting men
decisions.reason: "Drawing the sword" describes men able to fight with a sword (Judges 8:10).

decisions.choice: through the enemy lines
decisions.reason: Readable says what Mesha tried to break through.

source.text: וַיִּקַּח֩ אֶת־בְּנ֨וֹ הַבְּכ֜וֹר אֲשֶׁר־יִמְלֹ֣ךְ תַּחְתָּ֗יו וַיַּעֲלֵ֤הוּ עֹלָה֙ עַל־הַ֣חֹמָ֔ה וַיְהִ֥י קֶצֶף־גָּד֖וֹל עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיִּסְעוּ֙ מֵֽעָלָ֔יו וַיָּשֻׁ֖בוּ לָאָֽרֶץ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And he took his son the firstborn who would reign in his place, and he offered him up [as] a burnt offering on the wall; and was great wrath against Israel, and they set out from against him and returned to the land.

en.L: And he took his firstborn son, who was to reign in his place, and offered him up [as] a burnt offering on the wall. And there was great wrath against Israel, and they set out from against him and returned to [their] land.
en.B: Then he took his firstborn son, who was to become king after him, and offered him as a burnt offering on the wall. And great wrath came against Israel, so they withdrew from him and returned to their own land.
en.R: Then the king of Moab took his oldest son, the one who was to be king after him, and sacrificed him as a burnt offering on top of the city wall. Great anger came against Israel. So the Israelites left the king of Moab and went back to their own land.

decisions.choice: he offered his firstborn son as a burnt offering on the wall: a human sacrifice in sight of the besiegers
decisions.reason: Mesha offered the heir to his throne, most likely to Chemosh, the god of Moab (1 Kings 11:7), in a last plea for help. He did it on the city wall, where the armies outside could see it. The law of Israel condemned such sacrifices (Leviticus 18:21; Deuteronomy 12:31).

decisions.choice: there was great wrath against Israel: whose wrath is not said
alternatives: the Moabites' fury rose against Israel
decisions.reason: The word for wrath is used most often of God's anger (Numbers 1:53; 18:5; Joshua 22:20). Here the text does not say whose wrath it was. It may be Yahweh's anger against Israel, perhaps for driving Mesha to this act or for going beyond what Yahweh had said; it may be the fury of the Moabites, roused by the sacrifice; or it may be that Israel was struck with horror and dismay. The writer does not suggest that Chemosh had power. Israel's withdrawal follows directly.

decisions.choice: they set out from against him: the allies broke off the siege
decisions.reason: "Set out" is used for breaking camp. The allies left Mesha and his city and went home without taking Moab back.

decisions.choice: to the land: to their own land
decisions.reason: "The land" means each army's own country.

decisions.choice: wrath (Literal, Balanced); anger (Readable)
decisions.reason: Each level keeps the Hebrew open about whose wrath it was (m2). None of them names God or the Moabites.

decisions.choice: oldest son
decisions.reason: Readable says "oldest" for "firstborn" and names the king of Moab for clarity.
